events.continuity_hook: Starts a new family leisure episode after the December Denver work trip wraps up.
events.interaction_goal: Frame the D.C. weekend, compare the main airport and hotel-area choices, and identify the details Maya needs from her spouse before narrowing the shortlist.
events.scenario_brief: After the Denver workshop and before the holiday shutdown, Maya starts planning a Washington, D.C. family weekend for the January school break. The tentative plan is to fly from Atlanta on Saturday, January 17 and return Monday, January 19 with her spouse and child. She wants straightforward flights, ideally into Reagan National, and a well-rated hotel near Metro access and the museums, with breakfast included if it does not push the stay too far from the main sightseeing area. The open items are whether they can leave Friday evening instead, whether DCA is worth a fare premium over BWI, and which hotel neighborhood keeps the weekend simple without overspending.

events.continuity_hook: Continues the D.C. family weekend after the travel dates become firmer and the Friday option weakens.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the strongest flight-and-hotel combinations and choose the plan that best balances short-trip convenience, hotel comfort, breakfast, and Monday return timing.
events.scenario_brief: The school calendar confirms there is no Friday early release, and Maya's spouse cannot leave before late afternoon, making a Friday departure less useful. Saturday morning Atlanta-to-DCA nonstops are still reasonable, while the cheaper BWI options add more ground time than she wants for a short weekend. The hotel choice has narrowed to a strong-rated property near the Mall and Metro with paid breakfast, or a roomier suite hotel with included breakfast farther from the museums. Monday return options include a cheaper midday flight and a more convenient afternoon nonstop that allows a final museum visit. The unresolved pieces are whether to pay more for the hotel location and whether the family can get adjacent seats with Maya by a window.

events.continuity_hook: Final pre-trip check for the D.C. family weekend after flights and hotel are set.
events.interaction_goal: Create a concise family travel checklist and flag the last items to handle before leaving for the airport.
events.scenario_brief: A few days before the D.C. trip, the family has the Saturday morning ATL-to-DCA nonstop, the Monday afternoon return, and the Metro-adjacent hotel booked. Breakfast is not included at the hotel, but several nearby options open early. Cold rain is possible on Sunday, one museum still needs a timed-entry plan, and the room may not be ready when they arrive. Maya wants a final rundown for Atlanta airport timing, DCA-to-hotel transfer, luggage drop, dinner near the hotel, breakfast workarounds, museum timing, weather backup choices, and whether better adjacent or window seats have opened.

events.continuity_hook: Starts a new client work-travel episode after the family D.C. weekend.
events.interaction_goal: Frame the Philadelphia trip, identify workable flight windows and hotel areas, and list the client details needed before Maya sends a plan for approval.
events.scenario_brief: After returning from the D.C. weekend, Maya is assigned to a Philadelphia client kickoff scheduled for Monday, February 9 through Wednesday, February 11, with a possible Thursday governance meeting. The client may use either a University City hospital-campus office or a Center City meeting room, and the exact address is not yet confirmed. She wants Atlanta-to-Philadelphia flights that avoid unnecessary connections, a hotel with strong guest ratings, and a morning commute that will not complicate early client sessions. The unresolved details are the first required meeting time, whether Thursday attendance will be needed, and whether the client has a usable rate at a nearby hotel.

events.continuity_hook: Continues the Philadelphia planning after the client confirms the campus location and reduces the Monday arrival pressure.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the main flight-and-hotel packages, decide what to route for approval, and note how to handle the still-uncertain Thursday meeting.
events.scenario_brief: The client confirms the kickoff will be at the University City campus, with required sessions Tuesday and Wednesday from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Monday prep is now remote-only, so Maya can arrive Monday afternoon instead of Sunday night. Thursday's governance meeting is likely but still not final. The flight shortlist includes a Monday afternoon Delta nonstop into Philadelphia arriving before dinner and a cheaper one-stop itinerary that lands after 9:00 p.m. Return choices depend on the Thursday decision. Hotel options include a campus-adjacent property with a very strong guest rating and an on-site restaurant but paid breakfast, and an extended-stay hotel with included breakfast a longer walk away and mixed noise comments.

events.continuity_hook: Keeps the Philadelphia work trip moving after the Thursday meeting becomes definite and the return timing can be set.
events.interaction_goal: Finalize the Philadelphia booking plan, prepare the brief cost-and-commute explanation, and leave only routine seat and arrival details for a later check.
events.scenario_brief: The Thursday governance meeting is confirmed from 9:00 to 11:30 a.m., and Maya's manager approves the Monday afternoon nonstop and a Thursday afternoon return. The campus-adjacent hotel still has refundable rooms, but the rate has increased since the first search; the extended-stay option is cheaper but now only has a prepaid rate and several recent elevator complaints. Maya needs to decide whether to book the closer refundable hotel, add a quiet-room and luggage-hold request, note that breakfast will be paid separately, and check seat availability before the fares or room rates change again.
